notes.bbaasi: Un bus for town; un car or un autocar for long distances.
notes.paaka: La gare routière: the bus and taxi station.
notes.ntuuse: Je suis arrivé; a woman writes arrivée.
notes.tugende: Allons-y ! or, more casually, On y va !

guidebook.intro: Travel by taxi, bus, motorbike and plane. You’ll meet the future tense and the past with être.

tips.title: Je voyagerai: the future
body: The future adds endings to the verb’s dictionary form: **voyager → je voyagerai, tu voyageras, il voyagera, nous voyagerons, ils voyageront**. Some verbs have their own stem: **partir → nous partirons**, **aller → j’irai**.
For the near future, people often say **aller** + verb: **Je vais voyager demain** (I’m going to travel tomorrow).

tips.title: En bus, à moto
body: Travel by vehicle uses **en**: **en taxi, en bus, en voiture, en avion, en train**. If you sit on it, **à**: **à moto, à vélo**, and **à pied** for walking.
To take a vehicle: **prendre**: **Je prends le bus. Je prends un boda boda.**

tips.title: Je suis arrivé
body: To say something happened, verbs of movement use **être** + the past form: **Je suis arrivé** (I arrived), **Il est parti** (he left). The past form agrees like an adjective: a woman says **Je suis arrivée**.
**Désolé, je suis en retard !** (Sorry, I’m late!) is another useful one.

culture.title: La gare routière
body: Long-distance buses leave from **la gare routière**, often when they are full rather than on time. Ask **Il part à quelle heure ?** and expect the answer **Quand il sera plein**, when it’s full.
